stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor.
Suppose all finite limits exist in $\mathcal{A}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is left exact,
\item $F$ commutes with finite products and equalizers, and
\item $F$ transforms a final object of $\mathcal{A}$
into a final object of $\mathcal{B}$, and commutes with fibre products.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor and assume that all finite limits exist in $\mathcal A$.
conclusions:
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is left exact,
\item $F$ commutes with finite products and equalizers, and
\item $F$ transforms a final object of $\mathcal{A}$
into a final object of $\mathcal{B}$, and commutes with fibre products.
\end{enumerate}

reason: Equivalence proved by reduction to finite products/equalizers, a diagonal fibre-product expression for equalizers, and preservation of empty limits.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor.
Suppose all finite colimits exist in $\mathcal{A}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is right exact,
\item $F$ commutes with finite coproducts and coequalizers, and
\item $F$ transforms an initial object of $\mathcal{A}$
into an initial object of $\mathcal{B}$, and commutes with pushouts.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor and assume that all finite colimits exist in $\mathcal A$.
conclusions:
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is right exact,
\item $F$ commutes with finite coproducts and coequalizers, and
\item $F$ transforms an initial object of $\mathcal{A}$
into an initial object of $\mathcal{B}$, and commutes with pushouts.
\end{enumerate}

reason: Identifies statement as categorical dual to proved left-exact characterization; the dual implication is well specified.
